- **Date**: The race typically took place in April as part of the European cycling calendar
- **Category**: It was part of the UCI Europe Tour (2.1 category)
- **Location**: Various cities and towns across the Castilla y León autonomous community in northwestern Spain

## Race Format
- The race traditionally consisted of multiple stages over 3-4 days
- It typically included a mix of flat stages suitable for sprinters and hillier terrain that could favor climbers or punchy riders
- Often featured both road race stages and sometimes a time trial

## Significance
- Served as an important preparation race for riders building toward major spring classics or grand tours
- Part of the Spanish domestic cycling calendar
- Provided opportunities for both Spanish domestic teams and international UCI teams to compete

## Historical Context
The Vuelta a Castilla y León has been a regular fixture in Spanish cycling, though it has had various formats and categories over the years. The 2018 edition would have been part of the race's modern iteration as a UCI Europe Tour event.
